title: Bhola cyclone
summary: A cyclone struck what was then East Pakistan on 12-13 November 1970, its storm surge overwhelming low-lying islands and tidal flats. The World Meteorological Organization calls it the deadliest tropical cyclone on record, with an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 deaths; NOAA gives the same range and says census records did not exist, so the toll could only be roughly estimated.

uncertainty.note: WMO and Guinness give 12-13 November; NOAA gives landfall on the evening of 12 November.

where.modern_name: Bhola Island and the Bay of Bengal coast, Bangladesh
where.historical_name: Bhola island and coastal islands, East Pakistan

importance.justification: Recognised by the WMO as the deadliest tropical cyclone on record.

audience_note: Describes a mass-casualty natural disaster. Death tolls are estimates attributed to named bodies, not exact counts.
